verdicts.summary: The quit path does not 'keep running in the background and finish'. The forked close is interrupted when the layer scope closes right after the quit finalizer returns. Quit still progresses (markComplete fires), but the child-process teardown is cut short.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Quit while the primary backend's run-scope teardown is still pending at the 5s mark (child survives SIGKILL, or a later run-scope finalizer hangs). 2) stopAllPoolInstances -> primary.stop({timeout:5s}) forks the close into layerScope (DesktopBackendManager.ts:366) and times out; closeRun returns false and stop returns (1088-1090). 3) The quit finalizer returns, markComplete fires, scopedProgram's scope finishes (DesktopApp.ts:330-341). 4) program ends, so the Effect.provide layer scope closes (.repos/effect-smol/packages/effect/src/internal/layer.ts:15-21). The forkIn finalizer for the close fiber (.repos/effect-smol/packages/effect/src/internal/effect.ts:5370-5371) runs and interrupts it. 5) The interrupt reaches the child release (.repos/effect-smol/packages/platform/node-shared/src/NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:486-556). Its SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation (withTimeout, 402-435) and exit wait are interruptible and are abandoned. The run fiber and the instance's own stop() finalizer then run, but the close never completes. Consequence: a backend still tearing down at 5s is left with SIGTERM only, if SIGKILL had not yet fired. Grace is 2s (DesktopBackendManager.ts:67, 486), so SIGKILL normally fires before 5s and this bites only in the pathological case. The second teardown is not a hang: once run.fiber is interrupted, the second stop()'s Scope.close returns immediately (effect.ts:3780) and Fiber.await returns at once. The new test cannot see this because its parent scope stays open.
verdicts.consequence: Remaining run-scope teardown of a hung backend is abandoned at quit instead of completing. A child that has not yet received SIGKILL can be left with SIGTERM only. Quit itself still proceeds.

verdicts.summary: Same hazard as finding [0]: the mutex and the pre-timeout steps in stop() are unbounded. The note's WSL example is narrower than stated: the WSL helper calls in the start() config path are timeout-bounded. The unbounded residue is fs.exists and the blocking preflight dialog.
verdicts.scenario: WSL cold start: resolvePrimary -> wsl preWarm (10s timeout), wslpath (10s), distro/home probes (5s) and isAvailable (cached Effect.succeed) are all bounded, so the held mutex is released within tens of seconds, not indefinitely. Unbounded residue: fileSystem.exists(config.entryPath) (DesktopBackendManager.ts:725-727, no timeout, so a stalled share could hang), and onPreflightFailed showing a blocking showErrorBox (DesktopBackendPool.ts:255). Both sit before the 5s timeout in stop() (1051, 1077, 1081).

verdicts.summary: closeRun treats an interrupted close fiber as a successful close. If the instance's parent scope closes while the timed close runs, stop() goes on to cleanup while the run teardown is still incomplete.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A registered (WSL) instance has parentScope = its instanceScope (DesktopBackendPool.ts:342-345). 2) Quit calls stop({timeout:5s}), which forks the close into instanceScope (DesktopBackendManager.ts:366). 3) While it is pending, pool.unregister(id) closes instanceScope (DesktopBackendPool.ts:418-421). The forkIn finalizer interrupts the close fiber (effect.ts:5370). 4) Fiber.await returns an interrupted Exit rather than failing (Fiber.ts:59), so timeoutOption yields Some and closeRun returns true. 5) stop() runs cleanup: active is cleared, removeControlSource and discardSession run (DesktopBackendManager.ts:1091-1131), while run.scope's teardown was cut short and the child may still be alive. Requires an unregister overlapping quit, which I could not confirm happens in practice.
verdicts.consequence: Cleanup and state say the instance is gone while its child may still run during shutdown. The new timeout path on quit makes this reachable.
verdicts.missing: Whether pool.unregister can run concurrently with quit in practice. Only the unregister path was checked.

verdicts.summary: Pre-existing restart race that stop() does not guard against. A restart fiber that has already cleared restartFiber can run start() after stop() has returned, and start() re-arms desiredRunning and spawns a backend during quit.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The restart fiber's sleep ends and it clears restartFiber and reads desiredRunning=true (1016-1024). 2) Before it requests the mutex in start() (691-692), stop() acquires the mutex, sets desiredRunning=false, and captures restartFiber=None (1053-1070). 3) stop() returns, with active=None. 4) The restart fiber's start() takes the mutex. active is None and desiredRunning is false, so the early return at 695-703 does not fire. It sets desiredRunning=true unconditionally (732-738) and spawns a run (812-979). Result: a backend starts after quit has begun. The layer teardown interrupts run.fiber, or the process exits first and the child is orphaned. The window is narrow.
verdicts.consequence: A backend can be spawned during shutdown; it is either torn down by the layer scope or orphaned if the process exits first.
